sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Evolutionary Catalyst**: The Great Depression of 1929 and the success of Soviet Five-Year Plans inspired Indian intellectuals and industrialists to advocate for state-directed economic planning.
• **National Planning Committee (NPC)**: Formed in 1938 under the initiative of Subhas Chandra Bose and chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru to formulate a comprehensive national economic blueprint.
• **Ideological Spectrum**: Spanned from state-led heavy industrialization championed by capitalists to decentralized, village-centric self-sufficiency advocated by Gandhian economists.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Transition from laissez-faire colonial exploitation to indigenous, welfare-oriented, and industrial development paradigms.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Visvesvaraya Plan (1934)
Authored by M. Visvesvaraya; 'Planned Economy for India'; advocated democratic capitalism and rapid industrialization.
Shifting focus from agriculture to industry; doubling national income in a decade.
First systematic blueprint for Indian economic planning.
FICCI Proposal (1933-34)
Proposed by the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry; called for a National Economic Council.
Coordination of economic policies by Indian big business interests.
Highlights early proactive role of Indian capitalist class.
Congress Plan / NPC (1938)
Set up by Indian National Congress under Subhas Chandra Bose; chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru.
State ownership of key industries, land reform, and comprehensive national planning.
Established socialist leaning in Indian economic philosophy.
Bombay Plan (1944)
Authored by 8 leading industrialists (Tata, Birla, Dalmia, etc.); officially titled 'A Plan of Economic Development for India'.
Targeted a 3-fold increase in aggregate income and 5-fold in industrial output over 15 years; favored mixed economy.
Most influential capitalist blueprint shaping early independent planning.
Gandhian Plan (1944)
Authored by S.N. Agarwal; emphasized spiritual and moral progress alongside material self-sufficiency.
Focus on agriculture, cottage, and village industries rather than heavy machinery.
Represents anti-industrialization, decentralized Gandhian economic thought.

items.definition: Constituted in 1938 by the INC; created 29 sub-committees to study various economic sectors, though its final report was delayed due to WWII and the arrest of leaders.

items.term: A Plan of Economic Development for India (Bombay Plan)
items.definition: Published in two parts (1944 and 1945) by top industrialists; proposed a 15-year framework requiring Rs. 10,000 crores, heavily relying on deficit financing and foreign loans.
The ideological synthesis adopted by the Congress leadership combining state-directed heavy industry with democratic political structures and private enterprise.
Post-war Reconstruction Committee (1941), Advisory Planning Board (1946) headed by K.C. Neogy which recommended setting up a single permanent Planning Commission.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Industrial Hubs (Bombay/Calcutta/Madras)**: Center of gravity for the Bombay Plan and FICCI proposals, driven by indigenous merchant capital and port access.
• **Rural/Village Focus**: Gandhian Plan prioritized decentralized rural units across British India's agrarian hinterlands to eradicate rural poverty.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Colonial resistance, lack of capital, communal fragmentation, and divergence between capitalist goals and socialist ideals.
• **Policy Interventions**: Laid the intellectual groundwork for the Planning Commission (1950) and the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948.

items.title: Mnemonic for Chronological Order of Plans
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'Very Fast Congress Brings Growth' (VF-C-BG)
• **Decoded Meaning**: **V**isvesvaraya (1934) -> **F**ICCI Proposal (1934) -> **C**ongress Plan/NPC (1938) -> **B**ombay Plan (1944) -> **G**andhian Plan (1944).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly solves chronological arrangement questions without confusion.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Industrialists = Bombay (Capital/Heavy Industry); Agarwal = Gandhian (Village/Cottage); Visvesvaraya = Technocrat (Democratic Capitalism).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often states that the Bombay Plan was drafted or sponsored by the British Government. Clarification: It was entirely drafted by Indian private industrialists (Tata, Birla, etc.), though it aimed to influence post-independent India's governance.

Mains Value Addition: Quote the Bombay Plan in Mains answers on 'Inclusive Growth' or 'Public-Private Partnership' to demonstrate historical depth regarding Indian industrialists' early commitment to state-guided welfare and equitable distribution.

keyTakeaways: Economic planning in India predates independence, rooted in intellectual and industrial mobilization during the 1930s and 1940s.
The ideological clash between heavy industrialization (Bombay Plan) and rural decentralization (Gandhian Plan) shaped India's hybrid mixed-economy framework.
Chronology (Visvesvaraya -> FICCI -> NPC -> Bombay -> Gandhian) and authorship mapping are high-yield areas for UPSC Prelims.
